memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Methuselah had lived 187 years, he became the father of Lamech. After he became the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters. Altogether, Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died. - Gen 5:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Methuselah holds a record no one has ever broken - the longest human life in the Bible, 969 years. Yet even his story ends the same way as all the others: "and then he died." The longest life still came to an end. No number of years can defeat death; it only delays it.

But there is grace hidden even in Methuselah's long life. Many have noticed that his name and the timing of his life point to God's patience. His son was Lamech, and his grandson was Noah - and it was in the year of Methuselah's death that the great flood came. God stretched out this man's life to the very edge of judgement, giving the world centuries of extra time to turn back.

That is the heart of God. "The Lord is... patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance" (2 Pet 3:9). Every extra year Methuselah lived was another year of God's mercy holding back judgement.

The lesson for us is not to waste the time God's patience gives. The days we are granted are not accidents; they are opportunities of grace. God is patient, but patience is not permanence. Today, while there is still time, is the day to walk with Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you treating the time God gives you as an opportunity of grace?
- Is there any turning back to God you have been delaying?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Patient Father, thank You for the mercy of the time You give me. Help me not to waste it, but to turn to You and walk with You today.
